AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs deliver leadership AI and HPC performance enabling high density infrastructures with 288GB HBM3E memory, 8TB/s bandwidth, and expanded MXFP6 and MXFP4 datatype support.

Compared to Nvidia's B200 SMs, CDNA 4 CUs have half the per-clock throughput across many 16-bit/8-bit data types; AMD still relies on a bigger, higher-clocked GPU to keep an overall matrix throughput lead.
MI355X's HBM3E subsystem gives it 288GB capacity at 8 TB/s vs Nvidia B200's 180GB at 7.7 TB/s, maintaining AMD's memory capacity/bandwidth lead over Nvidia's largest GPU.
MI355X's lower CU count vs MI300X causes a slight vector performance reduction, but against Nvidia's Blackwell, AMD's higher core count and clocks still give it a huge vector throughput lead.

On every row the B300 beat the MI355X in a wafer.ai comparison; critics say the price comparison (MI355X at $2.5/hr) is unrealistic since no one is easily getting MI355X at that rate, and the B200 test unfairly spans two nodes with a cross-node all-reduce penalty.

Commenters called the wafer.ai MI355X vs B300 benchmark 'lazily written,' noting it never bothered to do TCO on actual ownership and relied on cherry-picked market prices to make AMD look cheaper per hour.

On the MI355X (288GB HBM3E) and MI325X announcement, a commenter noted AMD's pricing looks good vs Nvidia H100/B100 at around $15k, but expressed skepticism about AMD's consumer/compute software support translating to good experiences.
